newsitem.title: USA: Sentencing for Alabama mail bomber delayed.
newsitem.headline: Sentencing for Alabama mail bomber delayed.

text.p: Sentencing of the man who masterminded a wave of mail bombings that inflamed racial tensions in the South in 1989 was postponed indefinitely Monday, court officials said.

Walter Leroy Moody Jr. had been due to appear in Jefferson County Circuit Court Monday morning but no hearing was held. He faces a possible death sentence for the murder of a federal judge in Alabama.
"There's a lot of information that has to be compiled by the probation office and we do not have enough to sentence," judge's assistant Sue Hall told Reuters.
"We would expect to reset the hearing as soon as possible. We would hope that would be later this month," she said.

An Alabama jury in November convicted the 61-year-old Moody for the 1989 slaying of 11th U.S. Circuit Judge Robert Vance, who died while opening a package containing a bomb in his Mountain Brook home. The judge's wife, Helen Vance, was injured in the blast.
The jury recommended the death penalty to Judge William Rhea of Etowah County.

At the time of his state conviction, Moody already was serving life without parole on federal charges stemming from the murders of Vance and black civil rights attorney Robert Robinson in Savannah, Ga.
Prosecutors say Moody mailed out a total of four bombs from August to December 1989 after becoming frustrated by his own inability to overturn a 1972 conviction for possessing a pipe bomb.
The bomb that killed Robinson in December 1989 was meant to make police think a white supremacist group, such as the Ku Klux Klan, was behind the Vance murder.

Moody also mailed a bomb to the Jacksonville, Fla., office of the National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People. It was intercepted, along with a fourth device sent to the offices of the 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Atlanta.
State executions in Alabama are carried out by electric chair -- known to prison officials as "Yellow Mama."
